body: Eighteen of us, on a trip with Flamingo Tours, visited the picturesque Adisham bungalow, in the afternoon on 9th June 2023. After purchasing the entrance tickets, (Rs 100 local, Rs 300 foreign) we entered the most beautifully kept picturesque garden that I have seen for some time. There was a fairly large number of people enjoying the garden and taking photographs and selfies. There were some monkeys too entertaining the visitors with their pranks!Located 3 km from Haputale town and constructed in 1931, in typical British Tudor style, the bungalow was named after the English village 'Adhisham’, where the owner, Sir Thomas Villiers, was born in. His portrait, painted during 1930s greets you at the main entrance. It is owned by St. Benedict’s Monastery.The library, stocked with old volumes, and the sitting room are the only areas open to the public. Photographs are not permitted within the bungalow. The little kiosk by the side of the main building, sells a variety of fresh items from tea and coffee, homemade jams, pickles, and wines.After we spent about two hours within the premises, we left around 5 pm and walked back downhill to our hotel - about 3 km away.It was a most enjoyable trip.
title: Surrounded by Greenery - Lovely Garden

body: Heaven for Nature lovers.We stayed there for 4 days. it is an archaeological master peace. Built by a Scottish planter Sir Thomas Villiers in 1931, was told he wanted to have the weather as in Scotland. His wife was a painter and his picture painted by her is hanging there. Only part of the building is open to the public now. Beautifully standing with the majestic look on a cliff at the Thangamale National park at Haputhaleee, Sri Lanka.. Currently, it is owned by the Franciscan fathers. They are having a beautiful flower garden. There is a little chapel with prayers and Holy mass being said and you can participate.This is heaven for the bird watchers as we have recorded lots of endemic rare birds of Sri Lanka, There is a trade outlet where you can buy all types of jam and Vine made in the monastery itself. body: Only if you have enough time and happen to be in the area of Haputale on the opening days it is interesting to get an impression of the the life of a typical colonial lifestyle. The bungalow was built in 1931 by Sir Thomas Villiers on a perfect spot overlooking the mountains of southern Central Sri Lanka. His portrait hangs on the wall above the fire place in the living room; the old proud aristocrat Englishman being dressed in a European three parts suit. A video is recorded, but only in Sinhales (the overwhelming number of visitors are Sri Lankans). The building is fully constructed from big granite blocs and fits perfectly in its beautifully surrounding manicured gardens from where today's monks pick the fresh ingredients for their jams and cordials, which can be bought in the shop on the premises. It is now a Benedictine Monastery. Only two rooms of the former planter can be visited, the living room and the library, but with all furniture still in the original state you can get an impression of how this gentleman once lived. The back of the house is for the monks and not accessible to the public. The road towards the entrance gate winds through a lovely forested area.
title: Open only during weekends and public holidays

body: Adisham Monastery was the best experience in the three-day tour we had in Sri Lanka. The bus ride to Haputale from Nuara Elia was wonderful. Sights of the valleys below the cliffs of Haputale were stunning. We were travelling in Mistubishi Fuso Minibuses which could take the narrow one-way road to the Monastery from the main road.We reached at 4 p.m., just one hour before the doors were closing.The location, architecture and the surroundings would transport you to another place, another time. You feel like you are somewhere in Medieval Europe or Britain. When we reached the monastery, the weather was clear. As we grouped to take a photo, suddenly mist drifted in and we could hardly see anything. It stayed till we left. It was a great experinence.The monastery exhibits are limited in a few rooms, none of which you can touch or feel (expcet the furniture). Yet, it would tell you how a monastery is set up and run.The tea shop/sales counter offered great tea and food products from the Monastery, sold at a reasonable price. Most of us bought them.St.Benedict's Monastery (Adisham) is an absolute must visit place for any visitor to Sri Lanka.If you are transported on big buses, you may have to walk for about one kilometer from the main road to the Monastery on a narrow road.

title: Garden is beyond perfect

body: The facts are on the internet for everyone to find. But seeing the place in your own eyes, only makes you wonder, how could life ever be boring or sorrow if lived in a place like this. Being built on a flat piece of land on a mountain slope, on one side of the house is a steep mountain covered by tall green trees while on another side is a cliff providing a view stretching to distances beyond comprehension. The final result when those are combined with little bit of fog, is nothing but magnificent.Definitely a nice place to relax.The access road is quite narrow and poorly maintained. Could cause some trouble on crowded days.
title: Speaking of location for a home....

body: You can go to this place by taking a bus from Haputale and then walking through Thangamale sanctuary (1 km). Even though that bungalow is really amazing you can only view the library and lobby.But they are showing a video clip which takes a tour around the whole bungalow. The garden is nicely maintained with flowers and there is a shop to buy cordial and jam which is made in there farm.
title: Amazing bungalow but it is open

body: If I followed the instructions in Lonely Planet I would have never found it. Best is to take tuk tuk - you can agree with the driver to come and pick you up after a while. In a way there is not that much to see but the Monastery is just an oasis of peace. I sat under the tree and read a book for hours. Since is surrounded by trees it is a bit cooler and welcome addition to the humid and hot weather elsewhere. Reading stones with meaningful thought...well they made you think :)Great place for a little break from the buzzing other places and a bit of meditation. Beware of the cheeky and very brave monkeys at the entrance.
title: Europe in Sri Lanka

body: When I visited the monastery, it was raining hard and the bungalow was covered in the mist. You could easily think you were in the UK.It is a small monastery with a house, a shop, gardens and an orchard. Inside the house you are only allowed to see 2 rooms: the living room and the library. Next to the bungalow is a small shop selling homemade jams and jellies. Here and there in the gardens you see plates with motto’s like “Nothing works unless you do the work”. I didn’t see much of the orchard because of the rain and the clouds. Even with good weather the visit will not take more than 30 minutes, but the entrance fee is only 130 LKR. It is nice to visit when you are in Haputale, but don’t make a special detour for it.The monastery is only open on public holidays and the weekend. Inquire first at your guesthouse or hotel before heading off.
title: A monastery in the mist

body: Adisham bungalow located roughly 6-7 Km away from Haputale. It's a huge building constructed by one of the English land owner. It has huge walls made with stones. Most of the time the area covered with mist and in a sunny day you can have nice view around. Keep on mind since they have a monastery there it will open to public during weekends only.
title: Colonial Bungalow hidden in mist

body: Hidden in lush green and most of the time covered with mist it is a great place to visit.old colonial bungalow stands for decades with such glamour.presently handled by st.Benedict monastery.beautifully laid garden add glamour.
title: Majestic

body: This is a place where you can see a wonderful view of the land marks of srilanka when it's a clear sunny day this place is a old place where you can see some of historical things and most of the places are closed for visitors don't know why but it's a nice place to go
title: The grand Adisham

body: Open to public on weekends. Antique furniture and a fireplace. Next door is the all mechanical furnace supplying hot water as they did in the old days. There is the famous picture of the late Englishmen. Should go with family or friends cz there nothing else to entertain you. The view from North of the bungalow is epic. Adjoining structure is the commercial aspect of this outfit selling locally made Jam's and preserved fruits. Closest is from Haputale, but if you are coming from Nuwara Eliya from Boralanda junction. Roads are not that good but it is a scenic ride upto Boralanda and then up the Thangamale Estate. Last Visit 2012 may be..
title: Colonial Bungalow and Strawberries

body: I have been there before, and I know that there is nothing much to see. You can take some selfies being in front of the old rocky building and may be you can buy some fruit products. And be careful enough not to visit this place on week days. I went this time with my wife; and it was closed. So don't go there on week days.
title: Only on weekends

body: The place us nothing special and for the entrance you can just watch a movie about the monastery in sighala. Especially for europeans who know this kind of architecture from europe its nothing special
title: Nothing special not worth the entrance

body: Hidden away on top in the misty hills of Haputale, this is a monastery run by the Benedictine monks, which has been built by an former planter over a century ago. It is also a trip for local travelleres to get a glimpse of the surrounding mountain ranges. The monks operate a small store to sell tasty jams and preserves to visitors. It has limited accommodation facilities for pilgrims who wish to have a strictly religious holiday. Prior bookings are necessary and the procedure is complicated as a reference is necessary.
title: Monestery hidden in the hills

body: Awesome. ...... amazing European architecture built by the Scottish in Sri Lanka. ....... A must see after Horton Plains, Baker's Falls and the 'world's end' ........ gardens are beautiful too .....
title: 1600 Style Building completed in 1931

body: the monastery is only open to visitors during the weekends, poya days and school holidays. there is an entrance fee of 130LKR which goes to the maintenance of the place. indeed, it has a lovely manicured garden. only a small part of the building could be accessed by visitors and taking photos is not allowed. they have a video explaining the building's history and showing the other parts of the building off-limits to visitors.
title: lovely garden

body: You will feel that you are living in UK. Superb location. Wanna visit on and off. There are accommodation facilities avaiable in bungalow itself. Full greenery and seems like living in separate world.
title: Adisham bungalow

body: If you want to go and visit this place DO NOT FOLLOW route from Boralanda.Use bandarawela road otherwise you will really regret about poor infrastructure
title: Adisham

body: It is a old old building preserved with its own old furniture, painting and everything, well maintained and protected. It situated at a cool climate and has a nice garden.
title: Lovely place.....

body: Ancient Bungalow with a nice surrounding.Well maintained Garden.Fresh fruits and meat available.visiting in the morning would be best
title: Different kind of a Bungalow

body: There are only few places to visit in Haputale. This is one of the few places. Even though this is not a great place, in comparison to other similar places, I like few things especially the paintings, lovely garden and atmosphere. Max 1 hour tour is recommended.
title: Something is better than nothing

body: Can enjoy the garden, views of far mountains and also inside the bungalow. Better confirm before visiting because some parts are closed on some days inside the bungalow. I went on a weekday and I was allowed to see the part of the first floor only. Probably a weekend day would be better to see the best part inside the bungalow.
title: Great bungalow and a garden

body: Nicely maintain garden and bungalow. Play badminton there if you can. Loved the flowers and the garden. Might be congested with vehicles in weekends.
title: Lovely calm place

body: Old England style castle. Well maintain. Advice to park far and walk towards it. Vehicle going near the gates will cause you a loss of time to reverse and get back down. Gardens are well maintained.
title: Must see.

body: Nice location and beautiful surroundings, roses and flowers etc.However, much of the actual monastry was locked up and public not allowed in, so we ended up only watching a video of what is supposedly found inside.
title: Nice place!

body: Wonderful architecture of the building. Completely made by Basalt. It is closed for tourists on Good friday and Christmas days.
title: Historic Building.

body: Adisham bungalow is situated at the top of Haputale mountain with great surroundings. Whole area is very very misty all the time & having a very cool and wet whether condition. We just visited to see the monestary, so did not get the oppertunity to stay overnight.Whole place was seemed mysterious, scary and interesting...Wish to spend a night at Adisham....!!! Defenitly will be a great experience.
title: Wonderful... Mysterious...

body: Not that interesting. It's on the hill but views are mostly obstructed by vegetation and power lines. Garden was closed when we visited.
title: Only worth a visit if you have too much time

body: Its a great place for a couple to have a romantic walk. There is a small cafe to drink a coffee while the cold weather gives you a chill. must go place at haputale.
title: Nice place to relax

body: I loved this place. So much nature. Real forest as it was before colonial time. The garden is beautiful. Some fruit trees and lot of flowers in the garden. The monastery Looks like a Little Castle. Wish it would be mine. They have a Little Museum, 3 rooms of the owners Mr. Villiers. Also a shop with homemade products.
title: Cosy Castle - a must do!

body: As an European, the only interest in the place is to see something totally out of place; it is indeed a bit strange to find an-English looking manor (now monastery) with its garden an all in Sri Lanka. Both the few rooms and the video are quaint but just barely interesting and the views are nothing special. The only thing I thought worthwhile was to imagine how these landlords lived at the timeMany Sri Lankans around as it must be "different" for them.We did NOT try the jams, but they must be nice...
title: Visit only if you need to spend some time

body: And Poya days and some public holidays I think. There's not much to see up there. Just the monastery and a small rose garden.
title: Open only sat & sun

body: Plantation Bungalow turned Benedictine Monastery. Small section on display for visitors. Lovely garden. Small outlet selling home made Jan\ms and Fruit juices. Limited opening times. Call the place and find out.
title: ON the way.... attraction

body: With chill breeze and oversized roses, the place is one of the destination to watch when you are in Happutale. They have couple of rooms for accomodation and awaiting to exprience in my next visit. It has a clean view of the town from teh top and the Monsatery looks very beatutiful with the surroundings.
title: Romantic

body: Old British mansion. Now a monastery. Visitors can only enter into a restricted area and not the entire building.allowed area consist of the artefacts used by the British owner of the tea estate around . portrait in the visitors room said to be unique and it say when you look at from any angle his eyes are directly looking at you. It really didn't work for me. Try for your self.Though it is a monastery you would not see monks often since they are living beyond the restricted area. Beautifully kept lawn with rose bushes and other flowers. You can buy jams cordials etc produced at the monastery farm at a small shop. Some snacks and tea ,coffee etc available.
title: Old British mansion. Now a monastery

body: I thought I'd like to go here as this is the type of stuff I normally like. Only after driving for about 10 min up a twisting, winding road for a couple km, we found it was CLOSED. If you are planning on going, be aware it is only open on Sat, Sun, Poya Days and school holidays.
title: Disappointing

body: It was a bit surprising (and funny) to visit the 2 little rooms and the small garden of this monastery which make you feel in UK.But that's all. You can not visit any other part of the monastery (and those you are allowed to see are far to be stunning) and the jam shop is not very interesting...Go there only if you have 10 minutes to spend (travel time from Haputale not included).
title: A joke...

body: We went here straight from Liptons seat. Lovely views from the gardens but what a disappointment the bungalow is with only 3 small rooms open to the public. The so called café also fell well short of expectations. We enjoyed the walk back down the hill more than the Bungalow itself
title: The Adisham

body: Its a great place to see and visit, just a few kilometers..can walk..gave us a great feeling about its architectural values...
title: Must visit this place....

body: (+) good homemade jams, cordials and tasty fresh milk(+) scenic view(+) cheap entrance fee : 100 rupees(+ -) cute flower garden though not very big(- -) only 3 rooms can be visited in the house, doesn't include the monastery itself, doesn't include the church either...(-) no monks visible in public areas
title: Not much to see but beautiful

body: Its a colonial bungalow...very much British. It has a long history.The beautiful Garden, and the view breathtaking. The Farm shop is exclusive. You get good Jams and Cordials
title: Beautiful Place...

body: Ok, we had heard about this amazing place and trotted up the hill happily only to be told once we paid that we could only look in 2 or maybe 3 rooms which were is a sad state of repair, buy jam off them and well, stand in the garden... don't waste your time on this one!
title: Um.....why?

body: It really is a masterpiece of mansions built in a picturesque location that resembles British atmosphere. It really is mystique & soothing with plenty of greenery & flowers with pine fragrance all throughout. A MUST VISIT PLACE.
title: Another unique British Mansion with majestic old age taste.

body: I walked to there. It is a nice place to go in the morning. I arrived before it opens so I hiked the Tangamalai sanctuary as well. It needs 30 minutes to walk around only. If you stayed in Haputale, why don't you have a small walk there?
title: Worth to go if you stayed in Haputale

body: Nothing much to watch. There some tasty bottled fruit products to buy there like jam, chutney, cordial, etc.
title: Old but classic place

body: The monastery itself is impressive from the outside with a lovely garden and gorgeous views, but inside it was a bit like a dusty old museum with most of it roped off from the public. The best part was the walk up to the monastery through the forest reserve - lots of birds and beautiful old trees. Would recommend it for the walk and the lovely rest in the garden once you get to the top.
title: the walk through the forest is the best part

body: Rather a austere grey granite house, reminds me of Scotland or Yorkshire. Lovely building, wonderful views.As it is a practising Monastery you cannot see much of the interior but it gives you a good idea of how they lived in English Country splendor. The video they played in the first room I found interesting. As other reviewers have said it is only in English. Fine for me but not the many other nationalities visiting. Gardens are such a typical English Country look. Many plants you would see in a UK country garden and a few sub tropical additions. Well maintained and being freshly planted the day I visited. Nothing exceptional.Buy the marmalade !!!
title: If you are in the area go and see it

body: Visited with the family and enjoyed a lot. Bought marmalade made by monastery. Well maintained beautiful garden and its full of flowers. You feel like you are in a botanical/rose garden.
title: Wonderful place to visit

body: The exterior of the monastery is very impressive but once inside there isn't much to explore as the majority of it is closed off to tourists. The video playing in reception which is meant to give you a brief overview doesn't play in multiple languages so anything interesting from the history is lost for those that don't speak the local language.
title: Nice but limited

body: I have been visiting & staying at Adisham monastery since 1975. I generally stay for at least 5-6 days at a time. The jams, fruit cordials, strawberries offered are very tasty & no preservatives added.Only a few rooms are open to the public but I have had the honor of being able photograph every room. The food is great & the service gives me a feeling of living in a British country cottage. Adisham is a place to stay for at least a week to settle ones stressed mind with total relaxation. My family enjoyed our stays at Adisham & the assistance from the Benedictine monks. The sense of peace & harmony one experiences at Adisham is beyond imagination. My photographs were borrowed by the Friars to construct their website as I had access to the inner rooms. I hope these pictures will allow guest to see what the inner rooms look like as they are not permitted to visit these. I recomend that you need to visit Adisham at least once in a lifetime.
title: Lost in Heaven

body: A pretty depressing house with gloomy dark and grubby rooms. You can go into 3 rooms. We found the bookcase the most interesting bit. Very underwhelmed with the place if I am honest. Glad we only had a short drive to get here. However it did give an impression of how claustrophobic it must have been living in the hills in the 1890s.
title: Hope that this isn't how the locals think we live.

body: I have visited St Benedict's Monastery - Adisham several times, last time I visited was Feb 2012, But I must appreciate, the place is well kept. And every time I visit, I feel so relaxed and touched by the wonders of nature. Monastery is in the heart of foresty area, with misty road to flora and funa.. The side of the road to the Monastery is so nature oriented, and it's t he natural habitat!!Monestry grounds, has a area for the guest, where they show an introduction about the location which is very educative. In addition there is a outlet to sell naturally prepared Jam/Cordial and chutneys. This was the fav. place of my sister, since Stawberry Jam sold is delicious!~~If it's bit cold weather, you will be lucky to dine with a hot cup of coffee or tea from the mini resturent. My dear baby son loved the colourful flowers grown everywhere, and I must appreciate the successful effort the staff in maintaining the garden and the buildings to show the next generation about the history of values and religion~
title: Misty Monastery
wonderful walk in the rain to Adisham
body: i and my children took a leisurely 1 hr walk from haputale town to the monastery. enroute we enjoyed the views and mingled and chatted with the villagers . we also passed by the Thana.... bird scantuary where we heard distant gunshots. otherwise it was a peaceful and pleasant slightly gradient walk . it was a great feeling to have the winds and intermittent rain falling on us.... giving us renewed energy. along the way we took many photos of different types of wild flowers growing wildly on the road or in cottages. the monastry was about to close and we did a quick tour.. nothing much and came back by hitching a free ride from the workers lorry back to towm saving us some time and money. All in it was a relaxing trip and is recommended.

title: Charming Slice Of Scotland
body: This beautiful building with its well manicured lawns and well-kept gardens and stunning views make this an interesting place to visit. You only get to see a small section of the place, as this is a bona fide monastery. Buy some of the home-made jams, grown and made by the brothers in the monastery.

title: Grand old place
body: You have to pay an entrance fee of Rs. 25. Nothing much to see inside, expected more. the place is about 100 years old and the building still looks good. The gardens around it were well maintained.

title: Olde World
body: Haputale is a very cold station in the Sri Lanka map. It is reached by Train over a very scenic railway passing along many waterfalls, flora and climates and reaching over a 6000 ft altitude at one point over a gradient of 1 in 45 feet.By road too there are 2 very attractive routes via Balangoda or from the South thru Wellawaya and the Ella Pass.The Building dates back to the British Tea planting pioneers, one of whom Sir Thomas Villiers built this mansion of Stone with sprawling gardens. It is now a seminary fopr monks with a selected portion open to the visitors.

title: Beautiful building, not too much inside.
body: The outside architecture of the monastery is nice and well kept. It is worth a visit if you are in the area. There is very little of interest in the inside. They do not allow you to visit the area were the monks live. There is a small coffee stand, in the grounds, that serves delicious take away coffee and local snacks. We tried the fried "donut" looking savory snacks and found them fresh and delicious.

title: avoid on holidays
body: only limited rooms r open for viewing on sundays, public holidays and special days (eg. full moon days or easter) and since we went on a full moon day, we didn't get to see as much of the place as we wanted.

title: Not much to see
body: There is very little to see, actually. Only a couple of rooms where a cheesy reportage is shown on an old screen. The hike from Haputale is very pleasant, though.

title: A must see
body: The place is so nice and quiet with great view. beautiful drive up too. We took tuk tuk from Dias rest to there and it was well-worth it.

title: Must see if sleeping nearby
body: Given that there is not much to do, Haputale is definitely not the place to go out. Visiting the monastery takes maybe an hour, so nothing to fill the day. It looks differently in that it looks very european, kind of exotic in this place so I feel it is worth visiting. And it is cheap!
